newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end down, turnaround seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end down, turnaround seen soon.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower again Monday, in the wake of a slump in U.S. Treasuries, but traders were confident the market would perk up again soon.
"The bad news has been absorbed," said a trader at a local bank.
Traders said investors were largely absent Monday, waiting on the sidelines until the markets settle, leaving traders to drive the market lower in thin trade.
The market settled above the session's lows hit early on.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was down 3/8 at 74-3/8 after falling 1-1/4 on Friday, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.15 at 119.20.

Traders said the market was unruffled by an alliance announced Sunday between the center-left FREPASO party and the centrist Radicals, which completely changes Argentina's political panorama, reducing chances of the Peronist government of holding on to its majority in Congress at October's mid-term elections.
"Politics continue to be independent of the economy," said another trader.
In the money markets, the three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was flat at 7.0625 percent.
